visualReview.method: All16 current final-run frames individually opened and inspected with view_image; no early-run images reused.

views.notes: Original six-page PDF and approved corrected reference are visible together; zero and false remain readable. Stored split action appears in review.
Custom ranges omit page3; the additional five page credits and unchanged source history are disclosed next to the real PDF preview.
Tablet preview shows actual source page4 with document2 selected; two columns and page controls remain contained.
Tablet confirmation shows full source-retention and undo disclosure plus the explicit two-document, five-page create button.
Mobile Preview tab shows actual page4 selected by keyboard from document2; navigation and create action fit the narrow viewport.
Mobile Ranges view shows ranges, omitted page3, additional five credits, both children, retention disclosure and create action without horizontal overflow.
Lost-response warning and Check split result are visible immediately; the frozen selection remains intact and there is no new-request action.
Reopened saved operation displays the same accepted batch, no additional credit use, source link and explicit separate-new action.
Corrected approved child shows its own two-page PDF, source/root range1-2 and source download without replacing the original result.
Nested child visibly contains source page5, labeled local page1, immediate-source page2 of3 and root page5 of6; queued status is accurate.
Lost undo response shows precise removal/preservation disclosure and Check undo status for the same batch; no second mutation is required.
Undone receipt marks both direct children deleted while preserving source link and stating unchanged usage; historical status is explicit.
ZIP PDF leaf child renders source page2; its root is the two-page PDF and no ZIP-wide page numbering is implied.
Child of an uploaded split renders source page4; immediate page1 of3 and root page4 of6 are distinguished.
Authoritative policy rejection explains why no split was created. New split is disabled until PDF is restored in parser settings; subsequent reload/new request passed.
Mobile viewer can read the preserved original and historical split section; Split and Undo actions are absent.

limitations: Screenshots are actual scrolled viewports; the modal intentionally scrolls vertically and the mobile preview uses a separate tab.
Synthetic native-text PDFs and real local rules extraction; no hosted OCR, AI provider, production deployment or customer data involved.

errorResponseExplanation.reason: Each new immutable request is checked before submission. Seven preflight lookups returned404 because those request IDs did not yet have receipts.
The existing ZIP upload workflow checked its new request before importing the synthetic PDF leaf.
Two controlled lookup failures followed deliberately lost committed split and undo responses. Both operations recovered their exact saved result without duplicate mutation.

Parser PDF acceptance was deliberately disabled after the stored request was held. The actual server rejected that exact source/SHA/options request; its bound terminal record permitted a deliberate new operation after policy was restored.

Detail revalidation followed the deliberate workspace change before navigation completed. The new workspace cannot read the old document. The app moved to /app and the released old source response did not reopen the dialog or dispatch a split.
The harness discarded one actual committed split response and one actual committed undo response to prove uncertain-outcome recovery.

notes: Stored and upload splitting share the same declared flow component; no second state machine or inline component was added.
Flow identity includes user, workspace, parser, role, source ID and SHA. Commit-time cleanup aborts source requests and suppresses late UI continuations.
Page plans, costs, omissions, eligibility and labels are derived. Refs hold transient request and mount guards; immutable source bytes remain in component memory.
Persistent recovery contains only the scoped request binding and split options; compare-and-set guards prevent overwriting another saved request.
Source identity reads, receipt verification and mutation order have actual data dependencies. The fresh-actor check and isCurrent barriers prevent subsequent writes after scope replacement.

The nine real browser groups include repeated clicks, accepted-response loss, close/reload, failed undo confirmation, durable rejection and held-source workspace replacement; six dedicated helper tests exercise storage and scope cases.

limitations: Local compiled application and generated native-text PDFs; this is not hosted deployment or live OCR/AI provider evidence.
The normal rules extractor is used with real native PDF text. No extraction adapter supplies values and no provider is called.
The isolated browser rate-limit store avoids unrelated fixture interference; rate limiting is covered separately.

The browser covers native marker/range reuse, ordinary/ZIP/uploaded-split sources, nested lineage and source-preserving undo. Backend adversarial tests separately cover permission revocation during transactions and broader concurrency.
